annotation.title_clean: Study on an Operation Regulation Framework under International Humanitarian Law for Sentry Robots
annotation.title_en: Study on an Operation Regulation Framework under International Humanitarian Law for Sentry Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Tsujita, T.; Sakuma, Y.; Yamada, S.; Eto, R.; Kurosaki, M.
annotation.venue: Journal of the Robotics Society of Japan (JRSJ), Vol. 40 No. 7, pp. 651-654
named_instruments_referenced: Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions
annotation.summary_en: This paper by National Defense Academy of Japan researchers interprets articles of international humanitarian law (IHL), mainly Additional Protocol I. It proposes an operation regulation framework for sentry robots that protect civilians and parties to a conflict from suicide bombers. The framework turns the distinction, proportionality and precaution principles into legal indicators and is tested on a real robot with a terahertz camera and LiDAR.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes a framework for operating sentry robots in compliance with IHL
Turns the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution into legal indices: certainty, effort, nexus possibility, necessity and collateral damage
Interprets AP I Articles 48, 51 and 57 for robotic decision-making
Keeps a human in the loop for decisions about the use of force
Validates the framework experimentally on a Clearpath Husky robot with a THz camera and LiDAR
